STEP 1 - Scene: An airline-style meal tray (likely in-flight or hospital) with roast chicken slices, stir-fried noodles with meat and vegetables, plus a glass of water and a glass of dark soft drink. Only the two paper plates on the tray are part of the meal; the glasses are not food.

STEP 2 - Vessel: Two disposable paper plates. The right plate (noodles) appears about 20 cm diameter, area ≈ 314 cm². The left plate (chicken) appears about 15-16 cm diameter, area ≈ 190 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roast chicken slices (skin and white meat), left plate
- Stir-fried noodles (yellow egg noodles) with pork/beef pieces and vegetables, right plate

STEP 4 - Area:
- Chicken: covers about 45% of the left plate, roughly 85 cm² of the tray plates' area; relative to the 314 cm² reference, about 27%.
- Noodles: cover about 60% of the right plate, about 190 cm² (≈60% of 314 cm²).

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Chicken: 85 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 128 ml
- Noodles: 190 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 570 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Chicken: 128 ml × 0.9 ≈ 115 g
- Noodles (pasta-like, with meat and vegetables, mixed): 570 ml × 0.8 ≈ 456 g. Splitting the noodle dish: about 330 g noodles and 90 g meat/vegetable mix is a reasonable apportioning, but to keep it simple I treat the stir-fry as noodles (330 g) plus pork (90 g).

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Roast chicken (cooked, skin on): 115 g × 200 kcal/100g ≈ 230 kcal
- Stir-fried egg noodles: 330 g × 160 kcal/100g ≈ 528 kcal
- Pork/beef pieces with sauce: 90 g × 200 kcal/100g ≈ 180 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 535 g, ≈ 940 kcal. This is a plausible full airline or hospital main-course portion with noodles dominating, and the plate fill levels are consistent with the photo.
